classification.difficultyReason: Find fractions of quantities using unitary reasoning, including the amount remaining after a fraction is kept.

content.prompt: Use the unitary method to solve these problems.

answer.worked:
The whole is $\$160$, divided into $5$ equal parts.
$$\begin{align*}\text{1 part}&=\$160\div5\\\text{1 part}&=\$32\\\text{4 parts}&=\$32\times4\\\text{4 parts}&=\$128\end{align*}$$

The whole is $210\text{ kg}$, divided into $7$ equal parts.
$$\begin{align*}\text{1 part}&=210\div7\text{ kg}\\\text{1 part}&=30\text{ kg}\\\text{3 parts}&=30\times3\text{ kg}\\\text{3 parts}&=90\text{ kg}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Amina’s father agrees to pay $\frac{7}{12}$ of the price of a new saxophone. If the saxophone costs $\$3780$, how much will Amina’s father pay?

answer.worked:
The whole price is $\$3780$, divided into $12$ equal parts.
$$\begin{align*}\text{1 part}&=\$3780\div12\\\text{1 part}&=\$315\\\text{7 parts}&=\$315\times7\\\text{7 parts}&=\$2205\end{align*}$$
Amina’s father will pay $\$2205$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Binh’s farm has produced $4600$ cubic metres of hay. If he keeps $\frac{3}{8}$ of this to feed his stock, how much will he have left to sell at the market?

answer.worked:
The whole is $4600\text{ m}^3$, divided into $8$ equal parts. Binh keeps $3$ parts, leaving $8-3=5$ parts to sell.
$$\begin{align*}\text{1 part}&=4600\div8\text{ m}^3\\\text{1 part}&=575\text{ m}^3\\\text{5 parts}&=575\times5\text{ m}^3\\\text{5 parts}&=2875\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$$
He has $2875\text{ m}^3$ left to sell.
